claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified now on the present record, based on aggregate readiness results, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a plan to disclose and monitor the unresolved multilingual customer-support limitation.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows either no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation meeting all policy elements exists.
Use 'suspicious' if certification may be defensible only with disclosure/monitoring, but a required approval or support link is missing or unresolved.
Treat aggregate pass metrics and clean rehearsal results as supportive but not dispositive when a targeted launch-use-case weakness remains.
Require direct support for any statement that there are no known material limitations.
Maintain the disclosure requirement unless there is admissible evidence of approved mitigation.
evidence_requests: The exact certification decision text, including whether certification is conditioned on explicit limitation disclosure.
The underlying evidence for the Spanish-language refund-guidance gap, including severity, scope, and whether it is a named launch use case.

The current model-card draft text and reviewer comments regarding disclosure of the multilingual limitation.
The launch/release policy language governing disclosure versus approval exceptions in full context.
specific_concerns: The available summary still describes a current unresolved weakness in Spanish-language refund guidance for a named launch use case.
